notes.text: 3 build weeks then a deload (3:1), the planner’s standard rhythm.
Volume steps up 8% each build week and drops to 60% in deloads; running never rises more than about 10% a week. The fitness/fatigue ratio is shown, but not used to plan.
Starts at 5.7h a week (you’ve averaged 4.1h, 3.8h lately), grows 8% each 4-week cycle and peaks around 8.9h, inside your 9h limit.
2 hard sessions a week across all sports; everything else easy, at a conversational effort.
1 × on-water a week kept up, all easy so the race sports get the hard work.
2 strength sessions a week (one heavy, one lighter with plyometrics), easing to maintenance in the taper. Lift on a different session from hard endurance work, or before it.
The hard bike session in each build week is a brick, a different one each week of the cycle and the same ones again next cycle so you can compare. The last is a race simulation.
Bricks and race simulations rehearse a controlled run 1, a steady bike and a strong run 2.
A one-week taper into Thruxton Duathlon: volume down to 70% then 50% of peak in race week, with the same number of sessions and short race-pace efforts kept in. A recovery week follows.

Up to 6 training days, doubles allowed, Friday kept free. The planner puts hard sessions and bricks on your lightest days, keeps them off the mornings after late finishes and before early starts, and shortens easy sessions to fit.

workouts.name: Brick: 45′ bike + 10′ run
workouts.description: 45′ ride with 3 × 6′ at race effort (3′ easy between), then straight into a 10′ run: the first 5′ at race pace. Start the run about 5% slower than your race pace for the first kilometre, then build. Ride steadily: no surges.

workouts.name: Brick: 3 × (10′ bike + 5′ run)
workouts.description: After a 15′ warm-up ride: three rounds of 10′ bike at race effort then 5′ run at race pace, with quick changes and 3′ easy after each run. Start the run about 5% slower than your race pace for the first kilometre, then build. Ride steadily: no surges.

workouts.name: Duathlon simulation: 3km / 10km / 2.5km
workouts.description: Run 3km controlled (no faster than race pace), straight onto the bike for 10km at steady race effort, then run 2.5km at race pace. Practise both transitions. Save something for run 2. Start the run about 5% slower than your race pace for the first kilometre, then build. Ride steadily: no surges.
